## L1 Capability: Cloud and Infrastructure Security

Cloud and Infrastructure Security is the enterprise security capability that governs how cloud workloads, infrastructure configurations, and platform services are secured at the infrastructure and platform layer. Operating under the AWS shared responsibility model, this capability governs all Gainwell-owned responsibilities: configuration posture, identity and access for platform services, secrets lifecycle, workload runtime protection, data encryption, and vulnerability management. The capability provides the architectural constructs through which Gainwell enforces and continuously validates its cloud security baseline across all accounts, regions, and workload types. It is a cross-cutting platform capability that underpins the secure operation of all application and data workloads running in Gainwell's cloud environment.

## L2 Capability Areas

| L2 Capability | Description | Maturity |
|---|---|---|
| **Cloud Security Posture Management** | Continuous automated assessment of cloud account and service configurations against established security baselines (CIS Foundations Benchmark, HIPAA-aligned controls, enterprise policy). Detects configuration drift, enforces policy through AWS Config rules and SCPs, and provides a unified posture view across all accounts. | Developing |
| **Workload Protection** | Runtime threat detection and protection for cloud workloads — EC2 instances, ECS/EKS containers, and Lambda functions. Detects anomalous process behavior, unauthorized network communication, and credential access patterns at the workload layer using cloud-native and agent-based detection capabilities. | Initial |
| **Secrets Management** | Lifecycle governance for all infrastructure secrets: credentials, API keys, service account tokens, TLS certificates, and encryption key material. Provides centralized creation, access control, automated rotation, and audit for secrets consumed by cloud workloads and platform services. | Developing |
| **Cloud Identity and Access Management** | Governance of cloud-native platform identity: IAM role design, permission boundaries, Service Control Policies (SCPs), and least-privilege enforcement for AWS service and workload access. Distinct from enterprise human identity (Identity Security domain) — this capability governs what cloud services and workloads are permitted to do. | Developing |
| **Cloud Data Protection** | Encryption-at-rest governance for cloud-managed storage services (S3, RDS, EBS, DynamoDB, EFS). Governs customer-managed key (CMK) usage for PHI and sensitive data workloads, key rotation policy, and object storage access control (bucket policies, public access block, object ownership). | Defined |
| **Cloud Network Security Governance** | Policy compliance enforcement for cloud network configuration: security group rule governance, private endpoint adoption enforcement, VPC configuration assessment. Complements the Network Security domain's architectural design guidance by verifying that deployed configurations conform to the security baseline. | Initial |
| **Vulnerability Management** | Systematic identification, prioritization, and remediation tracking for infrastructure-layer vulnerabilities in cloud workloads — OS-level CVEs in EC2/ECS, container image vulnerabilities, and package-level vulnerabilities in Lambda functions. Governed by SLA-tiered remediation targets with pipeline-enforced deployment controls for unpatched critical findings. | Initial |
| **Inbound File Scanning** | Interception and malware/virus scanning of all inbound file streams at the ingest boundary before promotion to any destination storage volume (S3 buckets, EFS, databases). Enforces a fail-closed staging/landing zone pattern across all Platform Gainwell ingest channels — files are tagged with scan results and either promoted to their destination or quarantined, with real-time SOC alerting on infected content detection. | Initial |

## Capability Interaction Model

The seven L2 capabilities are mutually reinforcing and must be governed as an integrated architecture rather than independent controls:

- **CSPM** provides the unified visibility layer that detects failures across all other capability areas — a misconfigured IAM role, an unencrypted S3 bucket, or a publicly exposed security group will surface as a CSPM finding
- **Cloud IAM** governs which identities can reach secrets, keys, and workloads — least-privilege IAM policy is a prerequisite for the effectiveness of Secrets Management and Data Protection
- **Workload Protection** detects runtime threats that evade preventive controls — it is the last-resort detective layer when posture management and IAM governance have not prevented an exploit
- **Vulnerability Management** and **Workload Protection** are complementary: vulnerability management reduces the attack surface pre-deployment; workload protection detects exploitation of residual vulnerabilities at runtime
- **Cloud Data Protection** and **Secrets Management** both depend on **Cloud IAM** for access governance — key policies and secrets policies are IAM-layer controls

## Capability Maturity Reference

| Maturity Level | Definition |
|---|---|
| Initial | Ad-hoc; no documented process; reactive only |
| Developing | Process defined; inconsistently applied; limited automation |
| Defined | Documented, consistently applied; partial automation |
| Managed | Measured; automated enforcement; metrics tracked |
| Optimizing | Continuously improved; predictive; fully automated |
